what_its_for: Abacavir is used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus), the virus that can cause AIDS. It works by blocking the virus from making copies of itself in your body. This helps lower the amount of HIV in your blood, keeps your immune system stronger, and lowers your risk of getting HIV-related infections and complications. Abacavir does not cure HIV, but it helps you manage the disease.
how_to_take: Take abacavir exactly as your doctor prescribes. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. If you are using the liquid (oral solution), use the measuring device that comes with the medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember and to keep the drug working at a steady level in your body. Never stop taking abacavir without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 600 mg per day, which can be taken as one 600 mg tablet once daily OR as 300 mg twice daily (one tablet in the morning and one at night). For children, the dose is based on body weight and will be determined by the doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed. Missing doses can allow the virus to multiply and become harder to treat, so try your best to take every dose on time.
storage: Store abacavir tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed and away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. The oral liquid (solution) can be stored at room temperature or in the refrigerator — do NOT freeze it. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused medicine safely by asking your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT drink alcohol while taking abacavir. Alcohol can increase the amount of abacavir in your blood and raise your risk of serious side effects. Do not stop taking abacavir suddenly without your doctor's approval. Avoid sharing needles, razors, or toothbrushes, and practice safe sex, as abacavir does not prevent HIV from spreading to others. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you are taking this medicine before any procedures.
when_to_call_doctor: STOP taking abacavir and call your doctor or go to the emergency room RIGHT AWAY if you develop symptoms of a serious allergic reaction called Hypersensitivity Reaction. Signs include: fever, rash, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, extreme tiredness, body aches, shortness of breath, sore throat, or cough — especially if you have TWO OR MORE of these symptoms at the same time. Once you stop abacavir because of this reaction, NEVER take it again — restarting it after a reaction can be life-threatening. Also call your doctor if you notice: yellowing of your skin or eyes, unusual muscle pain or weakness, trouble breathing, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, or signs of too much acid in your blood (lactic acidosis) such as fast or difficult breathing and stomach discomfort.
when_it_works: Abacavir starts working right away, but it may take several weeks to months before you notice the full benefits. Your doctor will check your viral load (amount of HIV in your blood) and CD4 cell count regularly to see how well the medicine is working. Even if you feel fine, continue taking every dose as directed.
special_populations: GENETIC TESTING IS REQUIRED before starting abacavir. You must be tested for a gene called HLA-B*5701. People who have this gene are at very high risk for a serious, life-threatening allergic reaction and should NOT take abacavir. Pregnant women: Abacavir can be used during pregnancy if needed — talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking abacavir, as HIV can be passed to the baby through breast milk. Kidney disease: No dose adjustment is usually needed for mild kidney problems, but tell your doctor. Liver disease: Abacavir is NOT recommended if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Older adults: Use with caution — your doctor will monitor you closely.
